entries.title: Aftershock frays nerves as many Venezuelans left to fend for themselves
entries.snippet: In areas devastated by the twin earthquakes, people are using crowbars, pickaxes and their bare hands to try to reach survivors.

entries.title: 'No one move!': The agonising silence as Venezuela rescuers listen for survivors
entries.snippet: With tens of thousands of people still believed missing, teams listen for signs of life beneath the rubble.

entries.title: Six people shot dead at centre for mothers and children in Germany
entries.snippet: The male suspect who has been arrested was in a custody dispute over his baby daughter, police say.

entries.title: One big win and three defeats for Trump in dramatic day at Supreme Court
entries.snippet: While Trump celebrated a ruling expanding presidential power to remove and replace regulators, other decisions were major setbacks.

entries.title: US says it has agreed to 'stand down' after exchange of strikes with Iran
entries.snippet: A series of strikes over the weekend saw the US and Iran accuse each other of violating the ceasefire agreement.

entries.title: Pakistani strikes kill at least 28 civilians in Afghanistan, UN says
entries.snippet: Pakistan claims it was targeting militants near its border, but the Taliban government calls it an "atrocity".

entries.title: Putin makes rare admission of fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian strikes
entries.snippet: The Russian president acknowledged Ukraine's attacks were "obviously creating problems" but denied the shortages were "critical".

entries.title: South African leader warns anti-migrant protesters ahead of unofficial deadline
entries.snippet: Thousands of people from other African countries have left South Africa ahead of Tuesday's deadline set by anti-migrant groups.

entries.title: Osaka pays 'love and respect to Japan' in Wimbledon kimono
entries.snippet: Naomi Osaka has long been renowned for dazzling crowds with her on-court outfits - but making that compatible with Wimbledon's all-white dress code required special inspiration.

entries.title: Lilo & Stitch star Daveigh Chase's cause of death was Aids
entries.snippet: The actress, who also crawled out of a TV in horror film The Ring, passed away in LA this month, aged 35.

entries.title: DR Congo bans mass gatherings in the capital to prevent spread of Ebola
entries.snippet: Opposition politicians accuse the government of using the outbreak to halt a planned protest.

entries.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump's attempt to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
entries.snippet: The decision, seen as a win for central bank independence, sends the fight over removal back to the lower courts.

entries.title: South Korea football coach quits as president calls for probe into World Cup loss
entries.snippet: South Korea was eliminated after missing out on a spot among the eight best third-placed teams.

entries.title: 'You are Canadian heroes' - the forgotten hosts making World Cup history
entries.snippet: Canada are making history at this World Cup with a run that is likely to change the face of football in the country forever.

entries.title: Teyana Taylor's tears and Lauryn Hill tribute steal show at BET Awards
entries.snippet: Taylor had an emotional reaction to being presented with the Icon of the Year award by Janet Jackson.

entries.title: Fitness brand founder and Olympian Les Mills dies aged 91
entries.snippet: The Les Mills International brand is now known globally for choreographed workouts set to music, like Body Pump and Body Combat.

entries.title: Indian journalists condemn 'denial' of voting and passport rights of prominent editor
entries.snippet: Rajagopal has alleged that he has been unable to renew his passport after his name was deleted from the electoral rolls.

entries.title: Biden blasts Trump 'vanity projects', calling him a 'loser' at fundraising event
entries.snippet: The former US president took aim at his successor's projects in Washington DC, including a planned new White House ballroom.

entries.title: Europe's heatwave linked to 1,300 deaths, WHO says, as Germany hits record 41.7C
entries.snippet: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that Europe is not prepared for high temperatures.

entries.title: Senior South African police officer survives assassination attempt
entries.snippet: Deputy crime intelligence boss Maj-Gen Feroz Khan was due to appear before an inquiry into police corruption this week.

entries.title: Michigan governor threatens to pull troops from D.C. if used for Trump task force
entries.snippet: Michigan Gov. Whitmer is one of four Democrats who sent their states' National Guard troops to Washington, D.C. ahead of America 250 celebrations in recent weeks, amid President Trump's ongoing — and controversial — deployment in the city.

entries.title: Wheelchair users say private equity is making repairs harder
entries.snippet: People who rely on wheelchairs say that industry consolidation driven by private equity means long delays in getting them fixed, which isolates them from society and endangers their health.

entries.title: The Temporary Protected Status program may effectively be over. Here's what we know.
entries.snippet: A Supreme Court ruling gives the Trump administration space to strip this status from hundreds of thousands of more people from the few remaining countries with this program.

entries.title: Supreme Court takes sledgehammer to much of federal government's regulatory structure
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court struck down most of the limits that Congress and the courts had previously established to protect the independence of regulatory agencies that comprise much of the federal government.

entries.title: Venezuela's deadly quakes put its U.S.-backed government to the test
entries.snippet: Venezuela's La Guaira state bore the brunt of the earthquake damage, bringing memories of a 1999 disaster that became President Hugo Chávez's first major test. Now, it's the acting leader's challenge.

entries.title: Senate Ethics Committee dismisses complaint against Sen. Ruben Gallego
entries.snippet: The committee had been alerted by a fellow member of Congress of allegations of campaign finance violations and potential sexual misconduct, but said it found no evidence of wrongdoing.

entries.title: They were world-class tennis rivals. Now friends, they've teamed up against cancer
entries.snippet: They were the women's tennis champions of their generation. Now, Chris Evert and Martina Navratilova open up about friendship, cancer and retirement in the documentary Chris & Martina: The Final Set .

entries.title: Supreme Court restricts use of geofence warrants
entries.snippet: Writing for the 6-3 majority, Justice Elena Kagan said that the technique, known as geofencing, violates the Fourth Amendment's prohibition against unreasonable searches.

entries.title: Supreme Court says Fed's Lisa Cook can stay in her job for now
entries.snippet: The court's decision means Cook can stay in her position as her challenge to her dismissal plays out in the lower courts.

entries.title: Supreme Court cements Trump's power over agencies long considered independent
entries.snippet: In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court struck down a 91-year-old precedent that has prevented presidents from removing members of independent agencies meant to be a check on his power.

entries.title: FDA panel on peptides will include experts who promote the unproven chemicals favored by RFK Jr.
entries.snippet: The Food and Drug Administration is meeting next month to consider easing restrictions on several peptides, a group of unapproved drugs popular with followers of Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

entries.title: Professor known for 'torture memos' will advise conspiracy probe focused on perceived Trump foes
entries.snippet: John Yoo, a conservative law professor known for his views on presidential power, confirms he will advise a team investigating whether officials conspired against Donald Trump.

entries.title: What the Supreme Court rulings mean for presidential power
entries.snippet: The U.S. Supreme Court issued two major rulings on Monday that significantly expand presidential power and President Trump's attempt to further reshape the federal government. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Supreme Court analyst and SCOTUSblog co-founder Amy Howe.

entries.title: Supreme Court ruling proves Federal Reserve is unique agency, Lisa Cook's lawyer says
entries.snippet: In a 5-4 ruling, Supreme Court justices said that President Trump does not have the power to fire Lisa Cook, a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. Geoff Bennett discussed that decision with Cook's lead counsel, Abbe Lowell.

entries.title: Venezuela rescue efforts grow desperate as death toll rises and aftershock rattles country
entries.snippet: Venezuelans continued to search for loved ones trapped under debris and rubble caused by the devastating back-to-back earthquakes five days ago. The Venezuelan government updated the death toll, saying 1,700 people are dead. That number is expected to climb higher. Stephanie Sy r

entries.title: American dream slipping out of reach for many DACA recipients, new report finds

entries.title: Willy Vlautin on spotlighting working-class American life in his novels and music
entries.snippet: Novelist Willy Vlautin built his career writing about people on the edges of the American dream: working-class families, lonely alcoholics, and those struggling to make ends meet in the fast-changing American West. He's also a musician, telling his stories through song. Senior ar

entries.title: Live Results: Colorado midterm primaries
entries.snippet: The Democratic gubernatorial primary between U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet and state Attorney General Phil Weiser will not only determine who might lead Colorado, but it could also create an opening in the closely divided U.S. Senate.

entries.title: More than 100 Venezuelans who were deported from the U.S. hours before the earthquakes are missing
entries.snippet: A deportation flight from Miami arrived in Caracas hours before Wednesday's earthquakes. On board were 146 Venezuelans, including 19 women and seven children, according to ICE Flight Monitor.

entries.title: Sweltering Midwest heat cancels outdoor plans as cooling centers open and the East braces
entries.snippet: DES MOINES, Iowa — Summer camp and other outdoor activities were canceled or delayed Monday as a heat wave held its grip on the Midwest and spread eastward. Communities opened cooling centers and urged people to take it easy and stay hydrated. "Overall, we're looking at just a re

entries.title: Luigi Mangione gets stuck in elevator as judge delays his federal trial until January
entries.snippet: Luigi Mangione's federal trial in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson will now begin in January instead of the fall, a judge said Monday.

entries.title: D.C. will pay $50,000 to man detained while protesting guard patrol with 'Star Wars' song, record says
entries.snippet: A settlement document reveals the District of Columbia has agreed to pay $50,000 to resolve a lawsuit filed by a resident who accused police officers of illegally detaining him for following an Ohio National Guard patrol while playing Darth Vader's theme song from "Star Wars" on

entries.title: 3 firefighters killed in wildfires along Colorado-Utah border identified
entries.snippet: Federal officials say that the three firefighters killed over the weekend in a Colorado wildfire were part of a crew that goes into remote areas to quickly put out new fires.

entries.title: Former players Malik Beasley, Ed Davis charged in NBA gambling scandal
entries.snippet: Authorities say Beasley tailored his play while with the Milwaukee Bucks in 2024, based on bets on his performance, and others benefited, including Davis.

entries.title: Shooting at youth welfare facility in Germany leaves 6 dead
entries.snippet: Five people – four women and one man – died at the scene of the shooting in Stade, police said. A sixth, also an adult, died later at a hospital.

entries.title: America 250 brings extraordinary security challenge to Washington
entries.snippet: Hundreds of thousands are expected in Washington, D.C., for the 250th anniversary of the nation's freedom. Federal law enforcement is preparing for one of the city's largest security operations.

entries.title: UC Berkeley establishing Nancy Pelosi Institute dedicated to addressing democracy's challenges
entries.snippet: Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and the University of California, Berkeley, are partnering to form a new nonpartisan academic institute they say will be dedicated to strengthening democracy.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany: At least 6 killed in shooting in Stade
entries.snippet: Several people are reported dead following gunfire in the northern German city of Stade. Authorities arrested the suspected shooter and said the shooting concerned a custody dispute.

entries.title: Peru: Fujimori declared winner of presidential election
entries.snippet: After weeks of reviewing the ballots, Peru’s electoral commission declared Keiko Fujimori the winner of the presidential election.

entries.title: Alarm over alleged abuse in French schools and nurseries
entries.snippet: Hundreds of alleged cases of physical and sexual assault against children in French nurseries and elementary schools have revealed flaws in the system, experts say. They argue that reforms are urgently needed.

entries.title: Pride Month has great significance for those who feel invisible. In Slovenia, many LGBTQ+ people understand just what that means
entries.snippet: One of the first steps taken by Slovenia's new right-wing government in June was to remove the rainbow flag outside the Culture Ministry. As Pride Month draws to a close, DW surveys the situation of the LGBTQ+ community.

entries.title: US Supreme Court vastly expands Trump's presidential power
entries.snippet: The court reversed a 1935 precedent restricting presidential powers to remove heads of independent agencies. However, it barred Trump from firing Fed Governor Lisa Cook, preserving the central bank's independence.

entries.title: Poland orders Swedish submarines to bulk up navy
entries.snippet: Poland has placed an order for three Swedish submarines in an effort to step up defense capabilities. The NATO member is modernizing its navy in the face of Russian aggression at its borders.

entries.title: South Africa braces for anti-migrant protests
entries.snippet: Tensions are rising ahead of planned anti-migrant protests on June 30, as South Africa's government warns against violence. Analysts say deep social and economic crises are fueling unrest and xenophobia.

entries.title: EV myths muddy the road to electrification
entries.snippet: Claims that electric vehicle batteries are tainted by exploitative mineral supply chains are discrediting non-fossil cars as electrified road transport booms.

entries.title: UK-Africa relations: Starmer's 'reset' that never delivered
entries.snippet: Back in 2024, British Prime Minister Keir Starmer promised a fresh UK–Africa partnership. Two years later, his resignation leaves unfinished ambitions, scaled-back aid and questions about Britain's long-term commitment.

entries.title: US-India trade deal: Inside the key sticking points
entries.snippet: Both India and the US have signaled that the first phase of a landmark trade deal is close. DW looks at the main challenges in getting a deal past the finish line.

entries.title: Can Thailand, Cambodia unlock massive oil and gas reserves?
entries.snippet: An estimated $300 billion in oil and gas reserves is sitting under overlapping territory in the Gulf of Thailand. Cooperation on its extraction is complicated by political tensions over a separate land border dispute.

entries.title: EIB announces largest-ever loan: €3 billion to Airbus
entries.snippet: The European Investment Bank (EIB) has said the loan, the largest in its history, is aimed at helping boost the EU planemaker's research efforts. The money will be directed to commercial and defense projects.

entries.title: Venezuela earthquake: Aid ramps up as rescue window closes
entries.snippet: Venezuela was shaken by an aftershock on Monday as rescues continued. Interim president Delcy Rodriguez said she remained hopeful about rescue operations as criticism of her government grows. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Germany news: Temperatures plunge after historic heat wave
entries.snippet: A record-breaking heat wave has moved on, with temperatures sinking rapidly amid many storms. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is heading to Washington for talks with his US counterpart, with NATO issues in focus.

entries.title: Art biennial Manifesta revives Germany's postwar churches
entries.snippet: Following the destruction of World War II, around 1,000 new churches were built in Germany's Ruhr region. Today, many stand empty, but the contemporary art show Manifesta is giving them a new lease on life.

entries.title: Australia-Vanuatu deal bars foreign bases in island nation
entries.snippet: Australia and Vanuatu have signed a deal seen as a bid to check China's growing security presence in the region. But an economic deal between Vanuatu and China is still in the works.

entries.title: US, Iran deliver conflicting reports on fresh peace talks
entries.snippet: A US official said both the US and Iran have agreed to pause their attacks and allow vessels to move through the Strait of Hormuz. Technical talks between both sides are still to resume.

entries.title: Pakistan says it struck militant targets in Afghanistan
entries.snippet: The strikes come a day after an attack in the southern city of Karachi killed three paramilitary troops. Afghanistan's ruling Taliban condemned the "brutal" and "cowardly" strikes, saying they killed scores of civilians.

entries.title: Serbia: Protests continue after Vucic says he will step down
entries.snippet: Student-led demonstrations continued even after President Vucic announced his plan to resign within weeks. For more than 18 months, demonstrators have kept Vucic under pressure.
